problems.title: PCIe time
problems.statement: The simulator's PCIe: 25 GB/s per direction plus 1 µs per copy.

parts.prompt: Copy 100 MB host to device, in ms?

hints: Bytes / bandwidth, plus fixed cost per copy.
problems.solution: (a) 4.001 ms. (b) 4.010 ms: chunking costs only the per-copy overhead.

problems.title: Serial versus pipelined
problems.statement: Copy in 4 ms, compute 3 ms, copy out 4 ms for the whole job. Two copy engines (one per direction), one compute engine.

parts.prompt: Ideal pipelined time with many chunks, in ms?
With 4 chunks (fill + steady + drain ≈ max + (sum − max)/4), in ms?

hints: The slowest engine sets the steady state.
problems.solution: (a) 11 ms. (b) 4 ms. (c) about 5.75 ms: with 4 chunks, the first chunk's other stages and the last chunk's drain add a quarter of the rest.

problems.title: One copy engine
problems.statement: Same job on a GPU with a single copy engine shared by both directions.

options: the copy engine: 8 ms of copies must serialise

problems.solution: 8 ms of copies through one engine; compute (3 ms) hides behind them. Lab 7 prints your card's engine count for exactly this reason.

problems.title: Pinned memory
problems.statement: Pageable host memory goes through a staging copy into a pinned buffer before DMA.

parts.prompt: Why can't the GPU DMA directly from pageable memory?
options: The OS may move or swap pageable pages; DMA needs physical pages that stay put

parts.prompt: Can cudaMemcpyAsync from pageable memory overlap with kernels?
options: Generally no: it behaves synchronously through the staging buffer

problems.solution: DMA needs pinned (page-locked) memory; from pageable memory the driver stages synchronously, killing overlap. Pin the buffers you stream.

problems.title: How many chunks
problems.statement: Per chunk overhead: 1 µs per copy (2 copies) + 5 µs launch. Total data stages 4 + 3 + 4 ms as before, with two copy engines.

parts.prompt: Approximate time with k = 8 chunks, in ms?

problems.solution: (a) 4.93 ms. (b) 11.01 ms: too many chunks drown in overhead (and small kernels stop filling the GPU). The optimum is near $\sqrt{(\text{sum} - \max)/\text{overhead}} = \sqrt{7/0.007} \approx 32$.

problems.title: Stream semantics

options: Work within one stream runs in order
Work in different streams may overlap
Two kernels in different streams always run at the same time
The legacy default stream synchronises with other blocking streams

problems.solution: Streams allow overlap; whether it happens depends on resources. The legacy default stream implicitly orders with other streams, a common source of accidental serialisation (use per-thread default streams or non-blocking streams).

problems.title: A camera pipeline
problems.statement: Frames of 8 MB arrive at 60 fps. Upload at 12 GB/s, processing 6 ms on the GPU, results 1 MB downloaded.

parts.prompt: Upload time per frame, in ms?
Does a 2-stream pipeline keep up at 60 fps?
options: Yes: every stage is shorter than the 16.7 ms period

hints: Throughput is set by the slowest stage.
problems.solution: Period 16.7 ms; upload 0.67 ms, compute 6 ms, download ≈ 0.08 ms: all under the period, so a pipeline sustains 60 fps with latency ≈ the sum of stages (~6.8 ms).

problems.title: Events between streams
problems.statement: Stream A produces a buffer that a kernel in stream B consumes.

options: Record an event in A after the producer; cudaStreamWaitEvent(B, event) before the consumer

problems.solution: Events express the dependency on the GPU without stalling the host or other streams; a device-wide sync works but destroys overlap.

problems.title: Overlap ceiling
problems.statement: Ci = 2 ms, T = 10 ms, Co = 2 ms, many chunks, two copy engines.
problems.solution: 10 ms, 1.4×: when compute dominates, copies hide entirely, and the only further gain is a faster kernel. Overlap is worth most when the stages are balanced.

problems.title: CUDA Graphs
problems.statement: A pipeline launches 200 small operations per step.

options: per-launch CPU overhead, by submitting a recorded graph at once

problems.solution: Launch overhead. With many tiny operations per step it can be the difference between launch-bound and GPU-bound.
